residents.name: Mara Velez
residents.personality: Quietly observant, exacting about words and moderately untidy in physical space; she likes predictable mornings, soft lighting, and having several books open at once.

weekly_routine.activity: Edits manuscripts at home, usually with coffee and a printed style sheet beside her
Makes and eats a light lunch while listening to the radio
Continues editing and takes scheduled client calls
Finishes weekly invoices, backs up files, and clears the desk
Walks around the neighborhood to decompress
Does a short grocery run or picks up vegetables from the market
Changes bedding, waters balcony plants, and sorts laundry
Reads with breakfast and plans the coming editing week
Reads or watches a quiet program with Julian
Prepares meals and labels leftovers for the week

object_habits: My reading glasses live on the top of the nightstand by my bed, though I often carry them into the living room in their blue case.
I keep active manuscripts in a canvas folder on the bedroom desk and leave only the current proof pages on the desk surface.
My phone charges on the nightstand by the wardrobe, not beside the bed, because I do not want it within arm's reach overnight.
I put tea bags and the small brass spoon on the kitchen sink-cabinet countertop before starting work, then forget to put the spoon away.
When a book is in progress, I leave it face-down on the small shelving unit by the sofa with a receipt marking the page.

response_habits.trigger: When a client sends a rushed or contradictory revision request
response_habits.behavior: She closes the laptop, takes a brisk walk, and returns with a short written list of what actually needs doing.
She stops cooking and asks Julian to order noodles or makes toast with cheese.
She makes ginger tea, puts painkillers and water on the end table, and quietly checks his temperature.

response_habits.trigger: When someone interrupts a sentence she is editing
response_habits.behavior: She goes very still, rereads the sentence aloud, and answers more patiently than her expression suggests.

scheduled_stressors: Monday morning client deadlines and revision calls
Unpaid invoices she has to chase on Friday afternoons
The noisy recycling collection early on Wednesday mornings
residents.household: Mara and Julian are a long-term couple who share the apartment but sleep in separate bedrooms: Mara sleeps in the first bedroom and Julian sleeps in the second, which also serves as his office. Mara works mostly from home as an editor, while Julian commutes to a museum and uses the apartment's large living room for occasional evening project work.

residents.name: Julian Okafor
residents.personality: Sociable, practical, and enthusiastic about explaining how things work; he is good in a crisis but chronically leaves useful objects in the wrong room.

weekly_routine.activity: Shower, dress, and eat breakfast before commuting
Commutes to the museum
Coordinates loans, installers, schedules, and exhibition contractors
Commutes home and stops for small household purchases when needed
Stays late for gallery opening preparation or staff drinks
Cooks dinner while talking through the day's problems
Unwinds with music and a drink after the long museum day
Runs errands, collects parcels, and tidies the kitchen
Works on exhibition notes or repairs small household items
Cooks a large lunch and packs leftovers
Calls his mother and reads the weekend papers
Answers a few work messages, then prepares for bed

object_habits: My work badge and keys go into the shallow tray on the hallway storage cabinet's middle shelf as soon as I come home.
My museum laptop lives in my backpack, which I leave beside the desk in the second bedroom rather than on the desk surface.
I keep measuring tape, a multitool, and spare batteries in the upper drawer of the bedroom desk, even though Mara says the drawer is not a workshop.
I leave cooking oils and a wooden spoon on the kitchen island countertop while cooking and usually remember to clear them only after eating.
My weekend newspapers accumulate on the large sofa until Mara moves them to the living-room shelving unit.

response_habits.trigger: When a work problem becomes urgent
response_habits.behavior: He becomes unusually cheerful, makes a handwritten checklist, and starts calling people immediately.

response_habits.trigger: When he gets home after a late gallery setup
response_habits.behavior: He orders food, showers, and refuses to discuss the day until he has eaten.
He rearranges the dining table, fills the fridge with drinks, and puts music on far too early.

response_habits.trigger: When something in the apartment breaks
response_habits.behavior: He tries to repair it immediately, even if the correct response would be to call the landlord.

scheduled_stressors: Tuesday afternoon contractor meetings that regularly run late
Thursday deadlines for exhibition loan paperwork
Friday evening gallery openings and staff events
Saturday parcel deliveries arriving in several separate time windows
residents.household: Mara and Julian are a long-term couple who share the apartment but sleep in separate bedrooms: Mara sleeps in the first bedroom and Julian sleeps in the second, which also serves as his office. Mara works mostly from home as an editor, while Julian commutes to a museum and uses the apartment's large living room for occasional evening project work.

situations.what_it_is_like: One resident comes down with a short, ordinary illness and spends several days moving slowly, sleeping badly, and losing interest in conversation. Work becomes a source of guilt rather than focus. The well resident tries to be useful without hovering, while the sick one becomes unusually dependent and irritable about needing help.
situations.what_others_notice: The ill resident speaks less, pauses before standing, and seems embarrassed by how much the day has narrowed around basic comfort. The well resident becomes watchful and practical, checking in more often than usual and quietly taking over small decisions.

situations.what_it_is_like: Mara enters a concentrated stretch of work in which every sentence feels consequential and interruptions feel physically jarring. She is satisfied by progress but unable to feel finished, and ordinary social warmth gives way to clipped efficiency. She keeps thinking about unresolved passages even when she is meant to be resting.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian notices that Mara answers questions accurately but without her usual patience. She becomes very still while working, then suddenly paces or talks through a wording problem. Her tiredness shows more in her silence than in complaints.

situations.what_it_is_like: Julian has a demanding installation or exhibition deadline and spends long days coordinating other people's needs. He enjoys the urgency and the sense that a complicated plan is becoming real, but he comes home mentally crowded and continues solving problems after hours. He has little appetite for small domestic disagreements.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara sees him arrive animated but depleted, speaking quickly and retelling the day's crises as if they were entertaining anecdotes. He is more absent-minded than usual and can shift from cheerful to overwhelmed when one more request arrives.

situations.what_it_is_like: They have a friend over for an evening meal, and Julian takes pleasure in making the conversation lively while Mara listens closely and contributes precise, unexpectedly funny observations. Both enjoy the break from routine, though Mara begins monitoring the hour and Julian wishes the evening could keep going.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian seems more expansive and performative than usual, eager to tell stories and explain connections. Mara appears reserved at first, then grows warmer once she trusts the rhythm of the conversation; afterward she is socially full rather than energized.

situations.what_it_is_like: Julian has to stay at the museum late because a delivery, repair, or institutional decision goes wrong. He is frustrated by other people's delays but thrives when an actual problem needs solving. By the time he returns, he wants to recount everything and also wants not to be asked for anything further.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara notices a tired, overstimulated version of him: still talkative, but with a brittle edge and an unusually distracted gaze. He apologizes for being late before explaining the whole chain of events.

situations.what_it_is_like: A client or prospective project falls through after Mara has invested hope and careful thought. She tells herself it is ordinary freelance uncertainty, but spends several days questioning whether her exactness is valued. She becomes quieter and more self-protective while trying to regain momentum.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian sees her functioning normally but with less spark. She dismisses reassurance if it sounds generic, yet responds to specific recognition of her skill. Her attention keeps drifting toward the next possible piece of work.

situations.what_it_is_like: A relative visits or stays nearby, bringing affection, old stories, and a stream of practical opinions. Julian enjoys being the host and translator between family personalities, but feels pulled back into an older version of himself. He returns from family time both comforted and slightly raw.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara notices that Julian becomes more demonstrative and more easily teased. He talks on the phone longer, laughs louder, and becomes defensive if he feels she is judging family habits, even when she has said very little.

situations.what_it_is_like: A call with a parent begins as a routine check-in and turns toward health, money, or an old unresolved concern. Mara tries to sound calm and competent, then spends the rest of the day replaying one or two remarks. She wants closeness without being managed.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian can tell from Mara's careful tone that she is working hard not to sound upset. Afterward she becomes unusually exact about minor matters and may ask for quiet without explaining why.

situations.what_it_is_like: An unexpected outage interrupts both people's plans and makes the evening feel strangely unstructured. Mara is irritated by the loss of a predictable work rhythm, while Julian becomes interested in diagnosing the situation and reassuring her. Once the immediate inconvenience passes, both enjoy the enforced pause.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian becomes animated and competent, moving toward practical solutions. Mara initially looks tense and displaced, then softens when there is nothing left to optimize and lets herself be quietly companionable.

situations.what_it_is_like: Julian takes up a hands-on hobby connected to making, repairing, or learning a physical process. He is delighted by gradual improvement and wants to explain every discovery. The hobby gives him a satisfying counterweight to administrative museum work, though he sometimes overcommits.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara notices him becoming more patient with failure and more eager to share small successes. He has a fresh source of stories and enthusiasm, but can misread her quiet interest as an invitation to give a full lecture.

situations.what_it_is_like: Mara takes on a new regular client whose expectations are demanding but intellectually rewarding. She feels more professionally secure while also worrying that the client's urgency will consume the calm structure she relies on. She becomes preoccupied with proving herself before she has decided whether she likes them.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian sees more confidence in her professional talk and more guardedness around her free time. She is pleased when discussing the work but visibly bristles at vague requests and last-minute changes.

situations.what_it_is_like: A change at the museum alters Julian's commute or start time for the foreseeable future. The new schedule is manageable but removes some of the familiar transitions that helped him shift between work and home. He feels mildly resentful, then starts treating the inconvenience as a puzzle to solve.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara notices that Julian's energy arrives at different times and that he is less predictable about conversation. He is often brisk in the morning and oddly lively late at night, as though his day has been pushed out of alignment.

situations.what_it_is_like: Mara needs an uninterrupted stretch during a sensitive editing task, while Julian wants to talk through a problem or do evening project work. Neither feels unreasonable. The disagreement begins with logistics but touches a deeper fear: Mara worries her concentration is not respected, while Julian worries shared life is becoming a series of permissions.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara becomes precise and formal, explaining boundaries as if drafting a policy. Julian talks faster and gestures more, insisting he is only asking for a little flexibility. Afterward both are quieter and more careful than the argument itself seemed to require.

situations.what_it_is_like: One resident receives unusually specific praise at work, the kind that confirms a part of their identity they had begun to doubt. They feel pleased but suspicious of making too much of it. Sharing the news becomes an intimate test of whether the other person understands why it matters.
situations.what_others_notice: The praised resident tries to sound casual but returns to the subject more than once. Their posture is lighter and their attention more generous, even if they deny that the recognition affected them.

situations.what_it_is_like: They set aside time to examine shared expenses and upcoming costs. Mara wants clarity and dislikes surprises; Julian is comfortable with approximate plans until a number becomes urgent. The conversation is usually civil but leaves both aware of different ideas about security.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara asks focused questions and becomes tense when answers are vague. Julian tries to keep the mood easy, then grows more serious when he realizes reassurance is not the same as a plan.

situations.what_it_is_like: During a darker or more exhausting stretch of the year, Mara's energy drops without a single dramatic cause. Work takes longer, pleasures feel muted, and she becomes more protective of mornings. She knows the pattern and resents it, especially when Julian tries to cheer her out of it.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian sees her become slower to answer and less willing to make spontaneous plans. She is not openly distressed, but her usual sharp amusement is harder to reach and she spends longer in solitary concentration.

situations.what_it_is_like: A difficult exhibition opens successfully after weeks of friction. Julian feels proud, relieved, and strangely bereft now that the shared emergency is over. He wants to celebrate, but part of him is still waiting for something to go wrong.
situations.what_others_notice: He is unusually buoyant and generous, telling the same story from several angles. He seeks Mara's reaction more directly than usual and seems disappointed if she treats the success as simply another work event.

situations.what_it_is_like: Someone they care about needs a short-term place to stay after a disruption in their life. Julian immediately focuses on practical support, while Mara worries about privacy, disrupted sleep, and the emotional labor of being available. Both want to help, but they differ on how much structure the arrangement needs.
situations.what_others_notice: Julian becomes hospitable and solicitous, sometimes promising more than can comfortably be provided. Mara is courteous and attentive but more visibly guarded, watching for signs that a temporary arrangement is becoming indefinite.

situations.what_it_is_like: A holiday or family occasion creates competing expectations about where they should be and how long they should stay. Mara wants advance agreement and emotional breathing room; Julian is pulled toward spontaneity and inclusion. They enjoy parts of the occasion while privately tracking when they can return to their own rhythm.
situations.what_others_notice: Mara becomes more observant and economical with words as the social demand continues. Julian is outwardly warm and busy, but checks Mara's expression often and grows uneasy when she becomes too quiet.

small_disturbances.text: A parent calls with a question that was supposed to be quick but becomes emotionally complicated.
A colleague sends an urgent message about a museum problem that can wait, but feels as though it cannot.
A package arrives for the wrong resident and needs to be identified.
They realize there is no milk or other breakfast staple left.
A client changes the wording of a request after Mara has already begun working.
His commute is delayed by a service interruption.
A neighbor knocks to ask about an unfamiliar sound.
She wakes earlier than planned and cannot return to sleep.
He forgets an appointment until a reminder appears.
A brief internet failure interrupts work and conversation.
She discovers that a deadline was listed in a different time zone.
A relative asks him to settle a minor family disagreement.
Rain changes plans for the evening.
She receives an unexpectedly kind message from a former client.
A museum visitor or contractor remembers him from an earlier project and stops to talk.
The building's alarm briefly goes off without an apparent emergency.
A minor headache makes concentrated reading unusually difficult.
He realizes he has agreed to two social plans on the same evening.
